branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Residents still distrust the app for outage information, but practical harm from missing updates declines because another channel becomes authoritative.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Utility officials successfully bypass the app using alternate communication pathways.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint is contradicted if outage posts continue to be removed or remain effectively unreachable despite nominal policy changes.
endpoint_ledger.description: The platform resumes dependable public visibility for legitimate outage information on the main neighborhood app.
endpoint_ledger.label: Restored public outage channel on the app

meta.important_question: Will the neighborhood app visibly restore reliable public circulation of legitimate water outage information?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is the clearest terminal repair outcome implied by the scenario because the central failure is platform visibility of legitimate local information.
realization_criteria: Official outage updates and resident outage posts remain publicly visible on the app across repeated checks.
A visible moderation correction, exemption, or policy clarification is issued for outage-related content.
Resident exposure to utility_officials through neighborhood_app measurably rebounds from T0 levels.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: At T0 the channel is impaired but not irreversibly broken; correction remains plausible.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint is weakened if residents return to a single trusted source even if they still keep chats for social coordination.
endpoint_ledger.description: Residents continue relying primarily on rumor-prone private group chats and other fragmented pathways rather than returning to a shared public channel.
endpoint_ledger.label: Durable migration to fragmented off-platform information networks

meta.important_question: Will residents reconverge on a shared verified channel, or remain fragmented across rumor-heavy private chats and weakened public feeds?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly highlights shift to rumor-filled chats, making fragmentation a major endpoint option.
realization_criteria: A substantial resident subset continues to use private chats as the main outage-information source over multiple observed periods.
Public app discussion remains sparse, mistrusted, or ineffective for outage coordination.
Cross-resident disagreement about basic outage facts persists at a level consistent with fragmented common knowledge.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Migration has already begun at T0, but scale and durability are still unresolved.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint can coexist with continued app distrust; it is contradicted only if no alternate path attains meaningful reach.
endpoint_ledger.description: Utility officials establish an alternate reliable path to reach residents at meaningful scale even if the app remains partially impaired.
endpoint_ledger.label: Official distribution workaround established

meta.important_question: Will utility officials secure a workable distribution path that reaches residents at meaningful scale despite platform friction?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario implies platform ownership leverage over reach, so substitution is a distinct terminal possibility.
realization_criteria: Utility updates are repeatedly disseminated through a nonblocked channel with observable resident uptake.
Residents reference official guidance from alternate channels more often than rumor claims in outage-related discussion.
Operational communication from utility_officials no longer depends primarily on successful posting in the neighborhood app.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Officials are struggling at T0, indicating both need and incentive for substitution, but no successful workaround is yet evidenced.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint is not realized by mere investigation; it requires observable corrective response linked to accountability pressure.
endpoint_ledger.description: External scrutiny, especially local reporting, prompts the platform to acknowledge error and implement a corrective moderation response.
endpoint_ledger.label: Accountability-driven platform correction

meta.important_question: Will local reporting generate enough accountability pressure to produce a platform or moderation correction?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario specifically introduces reporters as a mechanism that may shift institutional behavior rather than merely describe events.
realization_criteria: Local reporting publishes verified findings on mistaken removals or communication failures.
Platform representatives or moderators issue a public acknowledgment, explanation, or corrective action traceable to the scrutiny.
Subsequent moderation behavior toward outage content changes in an observable and sustained way.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: An investigation is beginning at T0, but no public findings or platform response exist yet.

risk_flags.note: Population size and local network structure are inferred for simulation utility, not stated in the corpus.
Cause and reversibility of mistaken removals are under-specified, increasing uncertainty around correction speed.
Channel fragmentation may prevent residents from knowing what others know, amplifying rumor persistence beyond factual correction.
Utility communications appear dependent on external distribution channels they do not control.
Even if posts are restored, residents may not immediately return to the app without visible proof of reliability.

simulation_brief.summary: A fictional neighborhood app deploys automated moderation that incorrectly removes posts about a local water outage. Residents lose reliable visibility into outage information, some migrate to rumor-prone group chats, utility officials have difficulty distributing updates, volunteer or staff moderators face an appeals backlog, and local reporters begin investigating platform and information failures. T0 should preserve uncertainty around correction speed, trust repair, and whether residents reconverge on reliable channels or fragment further.
uncertainty_notes: No explicit city size or outage scale provided.
No named institutions or platform ownership structure provided.
Severity of actual water outage and moderation false-positive rate are not fully specified.

sociology_baseline.note: Residents are more likely to accept outage claims from familiar peers or already-trusted sources than from contested platform channels.
Visible evidence of widespread posting errors or credible media coverage could push more residents into complaint or channel-switching behavior.
Some residents remain quiet publicly due to uncertainty and limited confidence in any channel.
Private chat migration likely clusters around existing trust ties and neighborhood subgroups.
Belief in rumors or confidence in corrections may require repeated confirmation across multiple contacts or channels.
Neighborhood identity and institutional roles matter, but strong factional polarization is not yet fully formed at T0.
Attention is elevated at T0 because the outage is ongoing, but absent fresh signals some public attention may fade even before trust is repaired.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Legitimate outage posts being removed creates an information vacuum that increases receptivity to informal substitutes.
Residents are splitting between app-based public discussion and less-verifiable group chats.
Knowledge or perception of a moderation backlog reduces expectation of quick correction.
Utility officials have information but insufficient dependable distribution through the main local platform.
Local reporting may create a public focal point for verification and institutional response.
